source.title: Howe duality and dichotomy for exceptional theta correspondences
source.authors: Wee Teck Gan and Gordan Savin
readSections: The whole paper (§§1–15 and the references) in arXiv v1, 31 January 2021, 56 pp., the only arXiv version (https://arxiv.org/pdf/2102.00372v1; SHA-256 8b3b6702909a6a936e5984f46a3c2fbfe629b63db4ba0ae9bd4356286508c6e5; accessed 2026-09-22). Formulas at the recorded misprints were checked on page images.

The published version (Invent. Math. 232 (2023) 1–78; received 9 September 2021, accepted 15 September 2022) is closed access and was not read. Only its abstract, identical to v1's, was compared. The 2023 sequel cites '[GS, §3.5]' for the L-packet discussion that is §3.4 in v1, so the published numbering may differ.

The sequel, Gan–Savin, The local Langlands conjecture for G_2 (arXiv:2209.07346v2; Forum Math. Pi 11 (2023)): §2, its summary of this paper's results, and its citations of this paper, searched for corrections

summary: Gan and Savin study three exceptional theta correspondences over a p-adic field. They restrict the minimal representations of E_6^D, E_6 ⋊ Z/2Z and E_7 to the dual pairs PD^× × G_2, (PGL_3 ⋊ Z/2Z) × G_2 and G_2 × PGSp_6, D a cubic division algebra. They prove the Howe duality conjecture for all three (Theorem 1.2), and a dichotomy: every irreducible representation of G_2 lifts to exactly one of PD^× and PGSp_6 (Theorem 1.1). They determine the lifts of all non-supercuspidal representations and prove that the correspondences preserve temperedness and discrete series (Theorem 1.3). With no doubling see-saw available, the method is a 'ping-pong with periods'. Chains of containments between periods (the degenerate Fourier coefficients ψ_E of G_2, and Whittaker, Shalika and Fourier–Jacobi periods) close up through a see-saw with Spin_8^E and a Mackey analysis of its degenerate principal series (§§5–6, 11–12). Jacquet-module filtrations of the minimal representations handle the non-tempered and noncuspidal parts (§§13–14). The results are the input to the local Langlands correspondence for G_2 (PAPER-GAN-SAVIN-23-B). Tau Ceti has the split octonions, one library item, and its roadmaps plan the exceptional Lie algebras and the Chevalley groups. Smooth representation tools are planned in SmoothRepresentationsOfLocalGroups. Nothing plans minimal representations, exceptional dual pairs or the representation theory of p-adic G_2. Of 87 items, 1 is in the libraries, 2 are planned and 84 are missing. The missing items go to a new roadmap, ExceptionalThetaCorrespondencesForG2 (78), with sources for MP.3 (4, classical theta inputs), SR.3 (1) and ML.4 (1, the local Langlands correspondence for GSp_4). There are 22 source issues, recorded against arXiv v1: fifteen misprints, one error and six gaps. The error is that §9's 'Weyl-invariant quadratic form' is invariant on cocharacters, not on the characters it is written for. The gaps are unproved computations and cases left to the reader.

items.name: Theorem 1.1 = Theorem 6.1 (theta dichotomy)
items.statement: Let F be a nonarchimedean local field of characteristic 0 and π ∈ Irr(G_2(F)). Then π has nonzero theta lift to exactly one of PD^× (D a cubic division F-algebra) or PGSp_6(F).
items.note: Theta lifts are taken in the restriction of the minimal representation of E_6^D, respectively E_7, to the dual pairs PD^× × G_2 and G_2 × PGSp_6. Nontempered and generic π are handled by the Jacquet-module computations and [GS04, Cor. 20]; nongeneric tempered π by the see-saw of §5 and the chain of containments of Lemma 6.4.

items.name: Theorem 1.2 (Howe duality for the three dual pairs)
items.statement: The Howe duality conjecture holds for the dual pairs PD^× × G_2 ⊂ E_6^D, (PGL_3 ⋊ Z/2Z) × G_2 ⊂ E_6 ⋊ Z/2Z and G_2 × PGSp_6 ⊂ E_7: for π_1, π_2 ∈ Irr(G_2(F)), Θ(π_i) has finite length and dim Hom_{H_J}(θ(π_1), θ(π_2)) ≤ dim Hom_{G_2}(π_1, π_2); for τ ∈ Irr(H_J), Θ(τ) has finite length with a unique irreducible quotient (if nonzero). More precisely: (i) PD^× × G_2 gives an injection θ_D : Irr^♥(PD^×) ↪ Irr(G_2(F)), where Irr^♥(PD^×) is the set of representations with nonzero theta lift to G_2; if p ≠ 3 then Irr^♥(PD^×) = Irr(PD^×). (ii) (PGL_3 ⋊ Z/2Z) × G_2 gives an injection θ_B : Irr^♥(PGL_3(F) ⋊ Z/2Z) ↪ Irr(G_2(F)), the subset Irr^♥ can be determined explicitly, and the image of θ_B is disjoint from that of θ_D. (iii) G_2 × PGSp_6 gives an injection θ : Irr(G_2(F)) ∖ Im(θ_D) ↪ Irr(PGSp_6(F)).
items.locator: §1, Theorem 1.2; proved in §§7, 8, 12 and 15, pp. 2–52 (arXiv v1)
items.note: Assembled from Theorem 7.2 (PD^×), Theorem 8.5 (PGL_3 ⋊ Z/2Z) and Theorem 15.1 (PGSp_6). For τ ∈ Irr(PD^×), the nonvanishing of θ_D(τ) is equivalent to τ having nonzero vectors fixed by a maximal torus PE^×; for p ≠ 3 this is Lonka–Tandon (item lonka-tandon).

items.name: Theorem 1.3 (qualitative properties)
items.statement: The three theta correspondences (i) preserve tempered representations; (ii) any discrete series representation of G_2 lifts to a discrete series representation of precisely one of PD^×, PGL_3 ⋊ Z/2Z and PGSp_6; (iii) are functorial for non-tempered representations.
items.note: (i) is Lemma 6.3(i) with Theorems 8.2 and 14.1; (ii) is Corollary 15.7; (iii) is Theorem 15.1(v) and Theorem 8.2. For non-tempered representations 'functorial' means: the L-parameter of the lift is the composite of the L-parameter with the inclusion of dual groups (SL_3(C) ⊂ G_2(C) ⊂ Spin_7(C)).

items.name: Big theta lifts of generic supercuspidal representations of G_2
items.statement: Let π_gen be a Whittaker-generic supercuspidal representation of G_2 and Θ(π_gen) its big theta lift to PGSp_6. (a) If π_gen is not a theta lift from PGL_3(F) ⋊ Z/2Z, then Θ(π_gen) is an irreducible generic supercuspidal representation of PGSp_6. (b) Otherwise π_gen = θ_B(τ^ε) for a supercuspidal τ of PGL_3. (b1) If θ_B(Ind(τ)) = π_gen with τ ≇ τ^∨, then Θ(π_gen) ≅ Ind_{P_3}^{PGSp_6}(τ) ≅ Ind_{P_3}^{PGSp_6}(τ^∨), P_3 the maximal parabolic with Levi GL_3. (b2) If θ_B(τ^+) = π_gen with τ ≅ τ^∨, then θ_B(τ^−) = π_deg is an irreducible degenerate supercuspidal representation of G_2, Ind_{P_3}^{PGSp_6}(τ) = Ind(τ)_gen ⊕ Ind(τ)_deg, Θ(π_gen) ≅ Ind(τ)_gen and Θ(π_deg) ≅ Ind(τ)_deg.
items.note: Completes Savin–Weissman [SWe]. (a) is Corollary 12.5; (b) is Theorems 8.5 and 15.2.

items.name: The split octonion algebra
items.statement: O is the split octonion algebra over F: an 8-dimensional non-associative, non-commutative F-algebra with a conjugation x ↦ x̄, norm N(x) = x·x̄ = x̄·x and trace Tr(x) = x + x̄; N is a nondegenerate quadratic form. Every x ∈ O satisfies x² − Tr(x)x + N(x) = 0. A nonzero x is of rank 1 if N(x) = 0 and of rank 2 otherwise, in which case F[x] ≅ F[t]/(t² − Tr(x)t + N(x)) is a separable quadratic F-algebra. O_0 is the 7-dimensional subspace of trace-zero elements.
items.note: Tau Ceti (f790474) realizes the split octonions over any commutative ring as Zorn vector matrices, with conjugation, trace, the multiplicative norm (norm_mul), the alternative and Moufang laws, and the 7-dimensional imaginary part. The quadratic relation follows from conj_eq_trace_smul_one_sub and self_mul_conj. The rank-1 and rank-2 classification of elements is not stated in the library; it is elementary.

items.name: The exceptional group G_2 = Aut(O)
items.statement: G_2 is the automorphism group of the F-algebra O: a split simple linear algebraic group of rank 2, simply connected and adjoint. Relative to a maximal torus T in a Borel subgroup B, its simple roots are {α, β} with α short and β long, and the highest root is β_0 = 3α + 2β. Following Muić, T ≅ G_m² via t ↦ ((2α + β)(t), (α + β)(t)), so that a pair (χ_1, χ_2) of characters of F^× defines a character χ_1 × χ_2 of T.
items.note: The split group of type G_2 is a Chevalley–Demazure group scheme, planned in Reductive groups, Layer 9. Its Lie algebra as Der(O) is planned in LieHighestWeight, Layer 8 (Mathlib's LieAlgebra.g₂ is the Serre-construction quotient, with no structure theorems; Tau Ceti has derivation lemmas for Octonion). Neither plans the group G_2 = Aut(O) or its identification with the Chevalley group.

items.name: The maximal parabolic subgroups P and Q of G_2
items.statement: Let V_1 ⊂ V_2 ⊂ O_0 be subspaces of dimension 1 and 2 on which octonion multiplication vanishes, P = MN the stabilizer of V_2 and Q = LU that of V_1; P ∩ Q = B is a Borel subgroup. M ≅ GL(V_2) ≅ GL_2 with δ_P = |det|³; N is a 5-dimensional Heisenberg group with centre Z = U_{β_0}, M acts on N/Z by Sym³(F²) ⊗ det^{−1}, and the generic M(F)-orbits on N(F)/Z(F) are parametrized by the isomorphism classes of separable cubic F-algebras. L ≅ GL(V_3/V_1) ≅ GL_2 (V_3 = {x ∈ O_0 : xy = 0 for all y ∈ V_1}) with δ_Q = |det|^5; U is 5-dimensional and 3-step nilpotent, U = U_0 ⊃ U_1 ⊃ U_2 ⊃ U_3 = 1 with U_0/U_1 = U_α × U_{α+β} ≅ F², U_1/U_2 = U_{2α+β} ≅ det and U_2/U_3 = U_{β_0} × U_{β_0−β} ≅ F² ⊗ det as L-modules.

items.name: SL_3 and SU_3 inside G_2
items.statement: The subgroup of G_2 generated by the long root subgroups is isomorphic to SL_3; its normalizer is SL_3 ⋊ Z/2Z, the nontrivial element acting by a pinned outer automorphism. SL_3 is the pointwise stabilizer of a quadratic subalgebra of O isomorphic to F × F, and SL_3 ⋊ Z/2Z its setwise stabilizer. For a subalgebra isomorphic to a quadratic field K/F, the pointwise stabilizer is the quasi-split SU_3^K and the setwise stabilizer SU_3^K ⋊ Z/2Z.

items.name: Subgroups of the dual group G_2(C)
items.statement: The dual group of G_2 is G_2(C), which contains SO_3(C) ⊂ SL_3(C) ⊂ SL_3(C) ⋊ Z/2Z ⊂ G_2(C). The centralizer of SL_3(C) in G_2(C) is μ_3, and that of SO_3(C) is S_3 = μ_3 ⋊ Z/2Z. The centralizer of a long root SL_{2,l}(C) is a short root SL_{2,s}(C) and vice versa, giving SL_{2,l}(C) ×_{μ_2} SL_{2,s}(C) ≅ SO_4(C) ⊂ G_2(C).
items.note: Printed with 'SL_{2,r}(C)' for SL_{2,s}(C) (sourceIssues E1). Also used: G_2(C) ⊂ Spin_7(C), the dual of PGSp_6 (Theorem 15.1(v)).

items.name: Proposition 3.1 (Muić: principal series induced from P)
items.statement: For τ ∈ Irr(M) with central character ω_τ, let I_P(s, τ) = Ind_P^{G_2}(|det|^s τ) and J_P(s, τ) its Langlands quotient when it is a standard module. (i) For τ unitary supercuspidal, I_P(s, τ) is reducible if and only if τ^∨ ≅ τ and either ω_τ = 1 and s = 1/2, with a non-split sequence 0 → δ_P(τ) → I_P(1/2, τ) → J_P(1/2, τ) → 0 and δ_P(τ) generic discrete series; or ω_τ ≠ 1 and s = 0, with I_P(0, τ) = I_P(τ)_gen ⊕ I_P(τ)_deg. (ii) For τ = st_χ, I_P(s, τ) is irreducible except: χ = 1 and s = ±3/2 (0 → St_{G_2} → I_P(3/2, st) → J_P(3/2, st) → 0) or ±1/2 (I_P(1/2, st) of length 3 with unique submodule π_gen[1], generic discrete series, unique Langlands quotient J_P(1/2, st) and subquotient J_Q(1/2, st)); χ² = 1 ≠ χ and s = ±1/2 (0 → π_gen[χ] → I_P(1/2, st_χ) → J_P(1/2, st_χ) → 0); χ³ = 1 ≠ χ and s = ±1/2 (the same shape, with π_gen[χ] ≅ π_gen[χ^{−1}]). (iii) For τ = χ 1-dimensional unitary, I_P(s, τ) is irreducible except: χ = 1 and s = ±3/2 (0 → J_Q(5/2, st) → I_P(3/2, 1) → 1_{G_2} → 0) or ±1/2 (I_P(1/2, 1) of length 3 with unique submodule π_deg[1], a nongeneric discrete series, unique quotient J_Q(1, π(1, 1)) and subquotient J_Q(1/2, st)); χ² = 1 ≠ χ and s = ±1/2 (0 → J_Q(1/2, st_χ) → I_P(1/2, χ) → J_Q(1/2, π(1, χ)) → 0); χ³ = 1 ≠ χ and s = ±1/2 (0 → J_P(1/2, st_{χ^{−1}}) → I_P(1/2, χ) → J_Q(1/2, π(χ, χ^{−1})) → 0).
items.note: Due almost entirely to Muić ('The unitary dual of p-adic G_2', Duke Math. J. 90 (1997)). The last sequence is stated with the corrected middle term I_P(1/2, χ); the paper prints I_P(1/2, st_χ) (sourceIssues E3).

items.name: Proposition 3.2 (Muić: principal series induced from Q)
items.statement: For τ ∈ Irr(L) unitary with L-parameter φ_τ, let I_Q(s, τ) = Ind_Q^{G_2}(|det|^s τ) and J_Q(s, τ) its Langlands quotient. (i) For τ unitary supercuspidal, I_Q(s, τ) is reducible if and only if τ^∨ ≅ τ and either ω_τ = 1 and s = ±1/2 (0 → δ_Q(τ) → I_Q(1/2, τ) → J_Q(1/2, τ) → 0, δ_Q(τ) generic discrete series); or ω_τ ≠ 1 (τ dihedral), Im(φ_τ) = S_3 and s = ±1 (0 → π_gen[τ] → I_Q(1, τ) → J_Q(1, τ) → 0, π_gen[τ] generic discrete series); or ω_τ ≠ 1, Im(φ_τ) ≠ S_3 and s = 0 (I_Q(0, τ) = I_Q(τ)_gen ⊕ I_Q(τ)_deg). (ii) For τ = st_χ, I_Q(s, τ) is irreducible except: χ = 1 and s = ±5/2 (0 → St_{G_2} → I_Q(5/2, st) → J_Q(5/2, st) → 0) or ±1/2 (0 → π_gen[1] ⊕ π_deg[1] → I_Q(1/2, st) → J_Q(1/2, st) → 0); χ² = 1 ≠ χ and s = ±1/2 (0 → π_gen[χ] → I_Q(1/2, st_χ) → J_Q(1/2, st_χ) → 0). (iii) For τ = χ, I_Q(s, τ) is irreducible except: χ = 1 and s = ±5/2 (0 → J_P(3/2, st) → I_Q(5/2, 1) → 1_{G_2} → 0) or ±1/2 (I_Q(1/2, 1) of length 3 with unique submodule J_Q(1/2, st), unique quotient J_Q(1, π(1, 1)) and subquotient J_P(1/2, st)); χ² = 1 ≠ χ and s = ±1/2 (0 → J_P(1/2, st_χ) → I_Q(1/2, χ) → J_Q(1/2, π(1, χ)) → 0).
items.note: Due to Muić.

items.name: Proposition 3.3 (Borel principal series of G_2)
items.statement: Let β_1, β_2, β_3 be long roots with β_1 + β_2 + β_3 = 0 and, for a character χ of T, χ_i = χ ∘ β_i^∨ (so χ_1χ_2χ_3 = 1). Ind_B^{G_2}(χ) is irreducible unless χ_i = |·|^{±1} for some i or χ_i/χ_j = |·|^{±1} for some i ≠ j; or the χ_i are quadratic, nontrivial and pairwise different, in which case Ind_B^{G_2}(χ) = Ind(χ)_gen ⊕ Ind(χ)_deg with the first summand generic.
items.note: Due to Muić. §3.3 also records that a Langlands quotient π of I(s_1, s_2, χ_1, χ_2), s_1 ≥ s_2 ≥ 0, embeds in I(−s_1, −s_2, χ_1^{−1}, χ_2^{−1}) = I_P(π(χ_1^{−1}|·|^{−s_1}, χ_2^{−1}|·|^{−s_2})), and in I_P(−s + 1/2, χ_1^{−1}) when χ_1 = χ_2 and s_1 = s_2 + 1 ≥ 1.

items.name: Non-tempered irreducible representations of G_2
items.statement: Every irreducible non-tempered representation of G_2 is the unique irreducible quotient of exactly one of: (a) I_Q(τ) with τ an unramified twist of a tempered representation of L ≅ GL_2 with |ω_τ| = |·|^s, s > 0; (b) I_P(τ) with τ such a twist on M ≅ GL_2; (c) I_P(τ) with τ the unique quotient of a representation of GL_2 induced from characters χ_1, χ_2 with |χ_i| = |·|^{s_i}, s_1 > s_2 > 0. The quotients are written J_Q(τ) in case (a) and J_P(τ) in cases (b) and (c).
items.note: The Langlands classification for G_2, with Muić's results. Its analogue for PGSp_6 is item nontempered-pgsp6.

items.name: L-parameters and conjectural L-packets of G_2
items.statement: An L-parameter of G_2 is an admissible ϕ : WD_F → G_2(C), up to conjugacy, with component group A_ϕ = π_0(Z_{G_2}(ϕ)). Non-tempered irreducible representations are the Langlands quotients J_P(τ), J_Q(τ), J_B(χ), and get the parameter WD_F → M^∨ ↪ G_2(C) through the local Langlands correspondence for the Levi factor (singleton packets). Tempered non-square-integrable representations are summands of representations induced from discrete series of Levi factors; their packets have size 1 or 2 = |A_ϕ|, with the unique generic member attached to the trivial character. Discrete series parameters, by ϕ(SL_2): (1) principal SL_2: Π_ϕ = {St_{G_2}}; (2) subregular SO_3, with φ : W_F → S_3: φ trivial, Π_ϕ = {π_gen[1], π_deg[1], π_sc[1]} indexed by 1, r, ε of S_3 (π_sc[1] the depth-zero supercuspidal induced from the cuspidal unipotent representation G_2[1] of G_2(F_q)); φ(W_F) = μ_2, a quadratic χ, Π_ϕ = {π_gen[χ], π(−1)}, π(−1) = π_sc[−1] from G_2[−1] if χ is unramified; φ(W_F) = μ_3, a cubic χ, Π_ϕ = {π_gen[χ], π(ω), π(ω²)}, from G_2[ω], G_2[ω²] if χ is unramified; φ(W_F) = S_3, Π_ϕ = {π_gen[τ]}; (3) a short root SL_{2,s}, with φ : W_F → SL_{2,l} a supercuspidal τ of GL_2 with trivial central character: Π_ϕ = {δ_P(τ), π(−1)}, π(−1) supercuspidal; (4) a long root SL_{2,l}: Π_ϕ = {δ_Q(τ), π(−1)}; (5) ϕ(SL_2) = 1: supercuspidal packets.
items.note: A partial local Langlands correspondence (desiderata), not a theorem at this point; the queued PAPER-GAN-SAVIN-23-B proves the correspondence using this paper. In item (4) the paper calls SL_{2,s} 'a long root SL_2' (sourceIssues E2). The noncuspidal discrete series are all accounted for.

items.name: Local Fourier coefficients along N indexed by cubic algebras
items.statement: The M-orbits of 1-dimensional characters of N (the unipotent radical of P) are indexed by cubic F-algebras, the generic orbits by étale cubic algebras E; ψ_E denotes a character in the orbit of E, and π_{N,ψ_E} the twisted Jacquet module of a representation π of G_2.

items.name: Lemma 3.4 (nonvanishing and finiteness of degenerate coefficients)
items.statement: For every irreducible, nongeneric, infinite-dimensional representation π of G_2 there is an étale cubic F-algebra E with π_{N,ψ_E} ≠ 0; moreover π_{N,ψ_E} is finite-dimensional for every étale E.
items.note: Proof by citation: the wave-front set of such π is supported on subregular nilpotent orbits, parametrized by cubic étale algebras (Huang–Magaard–Savin; Loke–Savin); nonvanishing and finite-dimensionality are Mœglin–Waldspurger's theory of degenerate Whittaker models (Math. Z. 196 (1987)) and Varma's extension to residual characteristic 2 (Math. Z. 277 (2014)). These are general p-adic results that no layer of the atlas plans.

items.name: Freudenthal–Jordan algebras and the Lie algebras g_J
items.statement: Let J be a Freudenthal–Jordan F-algebra with cubic norm form N_J and M_J = {g ∈ GL(J) : N_J ∘ g = N_J}. The space g_J = sl_3 ⊕ Lie(M_J) ⊕ (F³ ⊗ J) ⊕ (F³ ⊗ J)^* carries the structure of a simple exceptional Lie algebra, of type G_2, D_4, E_6, E_7 for dim J = 1, 3, 9, 15. If dim J = 3, J is a cubic étale algebra E. If dim J = 9, J is the space of ι-symmetric elements of a central simple algebra B_K over an étale quadratic K with an involution ι of the second kind; the split case is J = M_3(F), with Aut(M_3) = PGL_3 ⋊ Z/2Z. If dim J = 15, J = H_3(B_F), the 3 × 3 Hermitian matrices over a quaternion algebra B_F, split when B_F = M_2(F). G_J is the identity component of Aut(g_J); for dim J = 9 there is a (not necessarily split) extension 1 → G_J → Aut(g_J) → Z/2Z → 1.
items.note: Following Gan–Savin, 'On minimal representations: definitions and properties' (Represent. Theory 9 (2005)) and Knus–Merkurjev–Rost–Tignol. LieHighestWeight Layer 8 plans explicit split E_6 and E_7 over a characteristic-0 field and names the magic square as one route, but not these forms over a p-adic field, the non-split E_6^D, or Aut(J). Tau Ceti's AlbertAlgebra is the 27-dimensional H_3(O), not used here. The paper writes the pair as (B_K, τ) and then the involution as ι (sourceIssues E4).

items.name: The dual pairs G_2 × Aut(J)
items.statement: The centralizer of Aut(J) in g_J is sl_3 ⊕ F³ ⊗ 1_J ⊕ (F³ ⊗ 1_J)^* = g_F, of type G_2, giving a dual pair G_2 × Aut(J) ⊂ Aut(G_J). For dim J = 9 there is an exact sequence 1 → Aut(J)⁰ → Aut(J) → Z/2Z → 1 with Aut(J)⁰ = PGU(B_K, ι), adjoint of type A_2. The cases used are H_J = Aut(J) = PD^× (J = D^+, D a cubic division algebra; G_J = E_6^D), PGL_3 ⋊ Z/2Z (J = M_3(F)^+; E_6 ⋊ Z/2Z) and PGSp_6 (J = H_3(M_2(F)); E_7), all groups of type E adjoint.

items.name: The dual pairs Aut(i : E → J) × G_E
items.statement: For an embedding i : E → J of a cubic étale algebra, H_{J,E} = Aut(i : E → J) ⊂ Aut(J) (for dim J = 9 its identity component is a 2-dimensional torus; see [GS14]). The centralizer of H_{J,E} in g_J contains g_E = sl_3 ⊕ t_E ⊕ F³ ⊗ E ⊕ (F³ ⊗ E)^*, t_E ≅ E^0 the trace-zero elements, which is Lie(G_E) for G_E = Spin_8^E, the simply connected quasi-split group attached to E; this gives a (non-injective) map H_{J,E} × G_E → Aut(G_J). H_{J,E} is PE^×, PE^× ⋊ Z/2Z and SL_2(E)/μ_2 for J = D^+, M_3(F)^+ and H_3(M_2(F)); for J = D^+, E is necessarily a field.

items.name: The see-saw (4.1) and the see-saw identity (5.1)
items.statement: The dual pairs G_2 × H_J and H_{J,E} × G_E form a see-saw in Aut(G_J): G_2 ⊂ G_E = Spin_8^E and H_{J,E} ⊂ H_J. For π ∈ Irr(G_2): Hom_{H_{J,E}}(Θ(π), C) ≅ Hom_{G_2}(R_J(E), π) (5.1), where R_J(E) = Θ(1) is the big theta lift of the trivial representation of H_{J,E} to Spin_8^E.
items.note: The diagram (4.1) prints G_E := Spin_4^E for Spin_8^E (sourceIssues E5).

items.name: Minimal representations and big theta lifts for exceptional dual pairs
items.statement: Π_J is the minimal representation of the adjoint group G_J (Gan–Savin 2005), extended to E_6 ⋊ Z/2Z so that Z/2Z fixes the spherical vector. For a dual pair G × H in G_J and π ∈ Irr(G), the maximal π-isotypic quotient of Π_J, Π/∩_{φ ∈ Hom_G(Π, π)} ker φ, is π ⊗ Θ(π) for a smooth representation Θ(π) of H (MVW, Lemme III.4); Θ(π) is the big theta lift and its cosocle (maximal semisimple quotient) θ(π). π has nonzero theta lift if Θ(π) ≠ 0, equivalently Hom_G(Π, π) ≠ 0; lifts from H to G are defined in the same way. Π_J is defined over R, so Θ(π̄) is the complex conjugate of Θ(π).
items.note: The minimal representations of E_6, E_6^D, E_7, Spin_8^E and SO_2n are inputs from Gan–Savin 2005, Magaard–Savin and Loke–Savin; nothing in the atlas plans minimal representations. MetaplecticAutomorphicForms MP.3 plans big theta modules only for the Weil representation of classical dual pairs.

items.name: Proposition 5.2 (R_J(E) and the degenerate principal series of Spin_8^E)
items.statement: Let P_E = M_E N_E ⊂ Spin_8^E be the Heisenberg parabolic, M_E ≅ GL_2(E)⁰, and I_E(s) = Ind_{P_E}^{Spin_8^E} |det|^s. Then R_J(E) ↪ I_E(s_J) with s_J = −1/2 for J = D^+ or M_3(F)^+ and s_J = 1/2 for J = H_3(M_2(F)). I_E(1/2) has length 3 if E is a field and length 2 otherwise, with a unique irreducible submodule V and quotient R_{M_3(F)}(E) ⊕ R_D(E) (R_D(E) = 0 if E is not a field); there are exact sequences 0 → R_{H_3(M_2(F))}(E) → I_E(1/2) → R_D(E) → 0 and 0 → V → R_{H_3(M_2(F))}(E) → R_{M_3(F)}(E) → 0. In particular I_E(1/2) = R_{H_3(M_2(F))}(E) if E is not a field.
items.note: Cited from Gan–Savin, 'A family of Arthur packets of triality Spin(8)', a 2015 preprint, and Segal (Trans. Amer. Math. Soc. 372 (2019)), for the module structure of I_E(s). A paper of Gan and Savin on Arthur packets for triality Spin_8 appeared in 2022 (Pure Appl. Math. Q. 18; arXiv:2106.06460); whether it contains the embedding R_J(E) ↪ I_E(s_J) as used was not checked.

items.name: Proposition 5.3 (vanishing of Ext¹)
items.statement: Assume E is a field. If π ∈ Irr(G_2) is tempered or has cuspidal support different from that of π_deg[1], then Ext¹_{G_2}(R_D(E), π) = 0, so 0 → Hom_{G_2}(R_D(E), π) → Hom_{G_2}(I_E(1/2), π) → Hom_{G_2}(R_{H_3(M_2(F))}(E), π) → 0 is exact.
items.note: As a G_2-module, R_D(E) is the direct sum of a supercuspidal representation (of infinite length) and π_deg[1], a constituent of I_Q(1/2, st) (Savin [Sa]); discrete series are projective in the category of tempered representations.

items.name: Proposition 5.4 (I_E(s) restricted to G_2)
items.statement: As a G_2-representation, I_E(s) has an equivariant filtration 0 ⊂ I_0 ⊂ I_1 ⊂ I_2 ⊂ I_3 ⊂ I_4 with I_0 ≅ ind_N^{G_2} ψ̄_E, I_1/I_0 ≅ I_P(s/2 + 1/4, C_c^∞(PGL_2)), I_2/I_1 ≅ m_E · I_P(s/2 + 1/4, ind_N^{PGL_2} ψ), I_3/I_2 ≅ m_E · I_Q(s + 1) and I_4/I_3 ≅ I_P(s + 1), where m_E = 3, 1, 0 for E = F³, F × K, a field. Hence 0 → ind_N^{G_2} ψ̄_E → I_E(s) → Σ_E(s) → 0 and an exact sequence 0 → Hom(Σ_E(s), π) → Hom(I_E(s), π) → Hom_N(π^∨, ψ_E) → Ext¹_{G_2}(Σ_E(s), π).
items.note: Mackey theory for the G_2-orbits on Spin_8^E/P_E. The paper calls it 'a key technical result' and gives no proof in arXiv v1 beyond the statement.

items.name: Proposition 5.5 and Lemma 5.6
items.statement: If π ∈ Irr(G_2) is tempered or has cuspidal support along Q, then Hom_{G_2}(I_E(1/2), π) ≅ Hom_N(π^∨, ψ_E). Lemma 5.6: for such π, Ext^i_{G_2}(J_j, π) = 0 for all i and all successive quotients J_j = I_j/I_{j−1} (j = 1, …, 4) of Proposition 5.4 at s = 1/2.
items.note: Proof of Lemma 5.6: second adjointness reduces to central characters; for tempered π the centre of M acts on r_P(π) by characters of absolute value |z|^t with t ≤ 0, while it acts on |det|^{1/2} C_c^∞(PGL_2) by |z|. The paper treats J_1 and says 'the other cases are dealt with in the same way'.

items.name: Lemma 6.2 (finiteness of the noncuspidal part)
items.statement: For each of the three J: (i) for π ∈ Irr(G_2), write Θ_J(π) = Θ_J(π)_c ⊕ Θ_J(π)_nc (cuspidal and noncuspidal components); then Θ_J(π)_nc has finite length, so Θ_J(π) has an irreducible quotient if nonzero. (ii) The same holds for τ ∈ Irr(H_J) and Θ_J(τ).
items.note: J = D^+ from Savin [Sa], J = M_3(F)^+ from [GS04], J = H_3(M_2(F)) from §§13–14. For H_J = PGSp_6 the tempered case is §14.2, and §14.3 treats Θ(σ)_nc only for the top pieces of the filtrations, 'leaving the details to the reader' (sourceIssues E12).

items.name: Lemma 6.3 (temperedness is preserved; non-tempered representations lift to PGSp_6)
items.statement: (i) If π ∈ Irr(G_2) and τ ∈ Irr(H_J) with π ⊗ τ a quotient of Π_J, then π is tempered if and only if τ is tempered. (ii) Every non-tempered π ∈ Irr(G_2) has nonzero theta lift to PGSp_6.
items.note: From Savin [Sa] (PD^×), [GS04] (PGL_3) and Theorem 14.1 (PGSp_6).

items.name: Lemma 6.4 (a chain of containments of periods)
items.statement: Let π ∈ Irr(G_2) be tempered and, for J = D^+, M_3(F) or H_3(M_2(F)), τ ∈ Irr(H_J) tempered with Hom_{G_2 × H_J}(Π_J, π ⊠ τ) ≠ 0. Then Hom_N(π, ψ_E) ⊆ Hom_N(Θ(τ), ψ_E) ≅ Hom_{H_{J,E}}(τ^∨, C) ⊆ Hom_{H_{J,E}}(Θ(π^∨), C) ≅ Hom_{G_2}(R_J(E), π^∨), and if one of these spaces is finite-dimensional all the inclusions are isomorphisms.
items.note: Uses (Π_J)_{N,ψ_E} ≅ ind_{H_{J,E}}^{H_J}(1) (item minimal-rep-coefficients), the see-saw identity, and Propositions 5.3 and 5.5, which give dim Hom(R_J(E), π^∨) ≤ dim Hom(I_E(1/2), π^∨) = dim Hom_N(π, ψ_E) (6.5). The first instance of the paper's 'ping-pong with periods'.

items.name: Proposition 6.6
items.statement: Let τ ∈ Irr(H_J) be tempered and π ∈ Irr(G_2) a tempered, non-generic quotient of Θ_J(τ). Then π is the unique irreducible tempered quotient of Θ_J(τ).

items.name: Proposition 6.7
items.statement: Let π ∈ Irr(G_2) be tempered and non-generic. Then Θ_J(π) cannot have two tempered irreducible quotients; in particular its cuspidal component Θ_J(π)_c is irreducible or 0.
items.note: Θ_J(π)_c is semisimple because the groups have compact centre (item cuspidal-semisimple).

items.name: Corollary 6.8
items.statement: Let π ∈ Irr(G_2) be tempered and non-generic. Then Θ_J(π) has finite length; if Θ_J(π) ≠ 0 it has a unique irreducible quotient θ(π), which is tempered; and for tempered non-generic π_1, π_2, θ(π_1) ≅ θ(π_2) implies π_1 ≅ π_2.

items.name: Proposition 7.1 (Savin: the dual pair PD^× × G_2)
items.statement: Let Π_D = ⊕_{τ ∈ Irr(PD^×)} τ ⊠ Θ(τ) be the minimal representation of E_6^D restricted to PD^× × G_2. (i) Θ(1) = π_deg[1]. (ii) For τ nontrivial, Θ(τ) is a nongeneric supercuspidal representation of finite length (possibly 0). (iii) For χ a nontrivial unramified cubic character, Θ(χ) = π_sc[χ] and Θ(χ²) = π_sc[χ²]. (iv) For each cubic field E/F, Hom_N(Θ(τ), ψ_E) ≅ Hom_{PE^×}(τ, C).
items.note: Savin, 'A class of supercuspidal representations of G_2(k)', Canad. Math. Bull. 42 (1999).

items.name: Theorem 7.2 (Howe duality for PD^× × G_2)
items.statement: (i) For τ ∈ Irr(PD^×), Θ(τ) is irreducible if nonzero. (ii) If Θ(τ_1) ≅ Θ(τ_2) ≠ 0 then τ_1 ≅ τ_2. (iii) If p ≠ 3, τ ↦ Θ(τ) is an injection Irr(PD^×) ↪ Irr(G_2). Hence dim Hom_{G_2}(θ(τ_1), θ(τ_2)) ≤ dim Hom_{PD^×}(τ_1, τ_2), and Θ(π) is irreducible or zero for every π ∈ Irr(G_2).
items.note: (i)–(ii) from Propositions 6.6 and 6.7; (iii) from Proposition 7.1(iv) and Lonka–Tandon. The paper labels the parts (i), (ii), (ii) (sourceIssues E6).

items.name: Torus-fixed vectors in representations of PD^× (Lonka–Tandon)
items.statement: If p ≠ 3, every irreducible representation τ of PD^× (D a cubic division algebra) has a nonzero vector fixed by PE^× for some cubic field E ⊂ D (Lonka–Tandon, J. Ramanujan Math. Soc. 33 (2018), Th. 2.4).
items.locator: §1 and proof of Theorem 7.2, pp. 2–23 (arXiv v1)
items.note: For p = 3 the question is open, which is why θ_D is only known to be injective on Irr^♥(PD^×).

items.name: Representations of PGL_3 ⋊ Z/2Z
items.statement: Z/2Z acts on GL_3 by the pinned automorphism A ↦ w_0 ᵗA^{−1} w_0^{−1}. For a Z/2Z-invariant Whittaker character ψ of the upper unipotent U, ψ ⊗ 1 and ψ ⊗ sign are its two extensions to U ⋊ Z/2Z. For τ ∈ Irr(PGL_3): if τ^∨ ≇ τ then τ^+ := Ind_{PGL_3}^H τ ≅ Ind τ^∨ is irreducible, and for generic τ it has one-dimensional (ψ ⊗ 1)- and (ψ ⊗ sign)-functionals; if τ ≅ τ^∨ it has two extensions differing by the sign character, τ^+ being the one with Hom_{U⋊Z/2Z}(τ^+, ψ ⊗ 1) one-dimensional when τ is generic. The only nongeneric self-dual representations are the Langlands quotients J_B(μ), μ = χ|·|^{1/2} ⊗ 1 ⊗ χ|·|^{−1/2} with χ² = 1, for which τ^± is fixed by θ(τ^+) = θ(τ) and θ(τ^−) = 0. Every irreducible representation of H = PGL_3 ⋊ Z/2Z is self-dual.

items.name: Lemma 8.1 (Whittaker and Fourier coefficients of the E_6 minimal representation)
items.statement: Let Π be the minimal representation of split E_6 ⋊ Z/2Z. (i) For a Whittaker character ψ_V of G_2, Π_{V,ψ_V} ≅ ind_{U ⋊ Z/2Z}^H(ψ ⊗ 1), so Hom_V(Θ(τ^ε), ψ_V) ≅ Hom_{U⋊Z/2Z}(τ^ε, ψ ⊗ 1). (ii) For an étale cubic algebra E, Hom_N(Θ(τ^ε), ψ_E) ≅ Hom_{PE^× ⋊ Z/2Z}(τ^ε, C).
items.note: 'Basic computations', not proved in the paper.

items.name: Theorem 8.2 (the results of [GS04] for PGL_3 × G_2)
items.statement: For τ ∈ Irr(PGL_3) with L-parameter φ_τ : WD_F → SL_3(C): if τ is non-supercuspidal then Θ(τ) has finite length; if τ ≇ τ^∨ is supercuspidal then Θ(τ) is irreducible supercuspidal (all τ are covered if p ≠ 2); θ(τ^ε) denotes the maximal semisimple quotient. (i) If τ ≠ τ^∨, θ(τ^+) is irreducible and nonzero; generic, supercuspidal, discrete series or tempered if τ is; if τ is not supercuspidal, neither is θ(τ^+), and its L-parameter is φ_τ composed with SL_3(C) ⊂ G_2(C). (ii) If τ = τ^∨ and φ_τ contains the trivial representation, θ(τ^−) = 0 and θ(τ^+) is irreducible, not discrete series, with parameter φ_τ composed with SL_3(C) ⊂ G_2(C). (iii) If τ = τ^∨ and φ_τ does not contain the trivial representation: for τ = St, θ(St^+) ⊕ θ(St^−) = π_gen[1] ⊕ π_sc[1]; for τ tempered induced from a supercuspidal σ ≅ σ^∨ of GL_2 with nontrivial central character, θ(τ^+) ⊕ θ(τ^−) = Ind_P^{G_2}(σ)_gen ⊕ Ind_P^{G_2}(σ)_deg; for τ a tempered principal series from nontrivial quadratic χ_1, χ_2, χ_3 with χ_1χ_2χ_3 = 1, θ(τ^+) ⊕ θ(τ^−) = Ind_B^{G_2}(χ)_gen ⊕ Ind_B^{G_2}(χ)_deg; for τ self-dual supercuspidal (p = 2), Θ(τ^ε) is supercuspidal and Θ(τ^+) ⊕ Θ(τ^−) = π_gen ⊕ π_deg with π_gen generic irreducible and π_deg nongeneric of unknown length.
items.note: Gan–Savin, 'Endoscopic lifts from PGL_3 to G_2', Compos. Math. 140 (2004), combined with §8.1. Self-dual supercuspidals of PGL_3 need p = 2: an irreducible 3-dimensional orthogonal parameter has primitive image A_4 or S_4, which needs wild ramification at 2.

items.name: Lemma 8.3 (a twisted Jacquet module of the E_6 minimal representation)
items.statement: Let ψ be a nontrivial character of [U, U], trivial on the centre Z_U of U (U the unipotent radical of Q). Then Π_{[U,U],ψ} ≅ ind_{GL_2 ⋊ Z/2Z}^{PGL_3 ⋊ Z/2Z}(C_c(M_2(F))) as (PGL_3 ⋊ Z/2Z) × SL_2-modules, SL_2 = [L, L], where C_c(M_2(F)) is the Weil representation of O_3 × SL_2 for the determinant form (GL_2 acting by conjugation, Z/2Z by X ↦ w ᵗX w^{−1}) and GL_2 ↪ PGL_3 by (a b; c d) ↦ (a 0 b; 0 1 0; c 0 d).
items.note: The paper says it 'follows by a standard computation' and gives none.

items.name: Proposition 8.4 (a miracle of Oberwolfach)
items.statement: Let τ ∈ Irr(PGL_3) be self-dual supercuspidal. Then Θ(τ^−) ≠ 0.
items.note: Proof: τ^− is a quotient of the SL_2-coinvariants of Π_{[U,U],ψ}, via Lemma 8.3, the even/odd Weil representations of S̃L_2 and their theta lifts to O_3 (item sl2-o3-theta), and the fact that every generic representation of GL_2, in particular st, is a quotient of τ|_{GL_2} (item prasad-restriction).

items.name: Theorem 8.5 (Howe duality for (PGL_3 ⋊ Z/2Z) × G_2)
items.statement: For τ ∈ Irr(PGL_3) with L-parameter φ_τ: (i) Θ(τ^ε) = 0 if and only if φ_τ contains the trivial representation (so τ ≅ τ^∨) and ε = −; (ii) Θ(τ^ε) has finite length with unique irreducible quotient θ(τ^ε) if nonzero; (iii) θ(τ^ε) is generic if and only if τ is generic and ε = +; (iv) if θ(τ^ε) ≠ 0 and τ is discrete series (resp. tempered), so is θ(τ^ε), and θ(τ^ε) is supercuspidal if and only if τ is supercuspidal or τ^ε = St^−; (v) θ(τ_1^{ε_1}) ≅ θ(τ_2^{ε_2}) ≠ 0 implies τ_1^{ε_1} = τ_2^{ε_2}. Hence dim Hom_{G_2}(θ(τ_1^{ε_1}), θ(τ_2^{ε_2})) ≤ dim Hom_{PGL_3⋊Z/2Z}(τ_1^{ε_1}, τ_2^{ε_2}), and for π ∈ Irr(G_2), Θ(π) has finite length with a unique irreducible quotient if nonzero.
items.note: The proof uses Lemma 8.1 (to put π_gen[1] into θ(St^+)), Proposition 6.6, Proposition 8.4, the Jacquet module of the E_7 minimal representation along P_3 (Magaard–Savin) and Savin–Weissman's result that a generic representation cannot lift to two different generic representations of PGSp_6. Two slips in the proof: E7 and E8.

items.name: Generic quotients of restrictions from GL_3 to GL_2
items.statement: Every generic irreducible representation of GL_2, in particular the Steinberg representation st, is a quotient of the restriction to GL_2 (embedded as in Lemma 8.3) of an irreducible generic representation τ of PGL_3.
items.note: Stated as 'it is known' without a reference. It is D. Prasad's theorem on GL_3 restricted to GL_2 (Duke Math. J. 69 (1993)), a case of the Gan–Gross–Prasad branching for GL.

items.name: PGSp_6, its action on ∧²F⁶ and its parabolic subgroups
items.statement: GSp_6 is the similitude group of the symplectic form with ω(e_1, e_6) = ω(e_2, e_5) = ω(e_3, e_4) = 1; P̃_1, P̃_2, P̃_3 are the stabilizers of ⟨e_1⟩ ⊂ ⟨e_1, e_2⟩ ⊂ ⟨e_1, e_2, e_3⟩ and P_i their images in PGSp_6. PGSp_6 acts faithfully on J = ∧²F⁶ ⊗ ν^{−1}: the group preserving the trilinear form ∧²F⁶ × ∧²F⁶ × ∧²F⁶ → ∧⁶F⁶ ≅ F is SL_6/μ_2, and PGSp_6 = Sp_6/μ_2 is the stabilizer of e = x_16 + x_25 + x_34 (x_ij = e_i ∧ e_j). M_3 = GL(⟨x_12, x_13, x_23⟩) ≅ GL_3 with δ_{P_3} = |det|²; M_13 = GL(⟨x_12, x_13⟩) × GL(⟨x_23⟩); P_2 is the stabilizer of the singular line ⟨x_12⟩, and M_2 ≅ (GL_2 × GL_2)/GL_1^∇ ≅ GSO_4 acts on V_4 = ⟨x_13, x_23, x_14, x_24⟩ ≅ M_2(F) by x ↦ α x ᵗβ, preserving 2 det(x) = (x, x, x_56), with δ_{P_2}(α, β) = |det(αβ)|^5; M_1 ≅ GSp_4 with δ_{P_1} = |ν|³.

items.name: Coordinates for the root system of PGSp_6
items.statement: With M_3 ≅ GL_3 the maximal torus is {(t_1, t_2, t_3)}; the simple coroots are α_1^∨(t) = (1, t, t^{−1}), α_2^∨(t) = (t, t^{−1}, 1), α_3^∨(t) = (1, t, t). An unramified character is χ(t) = |t_1|^{s_1}|t_2|^{s_2}|t_3|^{s_3}; the simple reflections for α_1, α_2 permute (s_1, s_2, s_3), that for α_3 is (s_1, s_2, s_3) ↦ (s_1 + s_2 + s_3, −s_3, −s_2); the root hyperplanes are s_i − s_j = 0 (short) and s_i + s_j = 0 (long); χ is in the positive chamber if and only if Re(s_1) > Re(s_2) > |Re(s_3)|. On this space of characters the Weyl-invariant quadratic form is s_1² + s_2² + s_3² + (s_1 + s_2 + s_3)², with simple roots (0, 1, −1), (1, −1, 0), (−1, 1, 1) of type C_3.
items.note: Stated here with the corrected invariant form and simple roots. The paper gives q = s_1² + s_2² + s_3³ − ¼(s_1 + s_2 + s_3)² with simple roots (0, 1, −1), (1, −1, 0), (0, 2, 2), which is the invariant form and root realization on the dual (cocharacter) space (sourceIssues E9); nothing later uses it.

items.name: Proposition 10.1 (principal series of PGSp_6 induced from P_2)
items.statement: For τ ∈ Irr(GL_2) with L-parameter φ_τ and central character ω_τ, let I_2(s, τ ⊗ τ) = Ind_{P_2}^{PGSp_6}((|det|^s τ) ⊗ (|det|^s τ)). (i) For τ unitary supercuspidal, it is reducible if and only if τ^∨ ≅ τ and either ω_τ = 1 and s = ±1/2 (0 → δ_2(τ) → I_2(1/2, τ ⊗ τ) → J_2(1/2, τ ⊗ τ) → 0, δ_2(τ) generic discrete series); or ω_τ ≠ 1, Im(φ_τ) = S_3, s = ±1 (0 → σ_gen[τ] → I_2(1, τ ⊗ τ) → J_2(1, τ ⊗ τ) → 0); or ω_τ ≠ 1, Im(φ_τ) ≠ S_3, s = 0 (I_2(0, τ ⊗ τ) = I_2(τ ⊗ τ)_gen ⊕ I_2(τ ⊗ τ)_deg). (ii) For τ = st_χ it is irreducible except: χ = 1 and s = ±5/2 (0 → St_{PGSp_6} → I_2(5/2, st ⊗ st) → J_2(5/2, st ⊗ st) → 0) or ±1/2 (0 → Ind_{P_3}^{PGSp_6}(St)_gen → I_2(1/2, st ⊗ st) → J_2(1/2, st ⊗ st) → 0); χ² = 1 ≠ χ and s = ±1/2 (0 → σ_gen[χ] → I_2(1/2, st_χ ⊗ st_χ) → J_2(1/2, st_χ ⊗ st_χ) → 0).
items.note: Reducibility points computed from L-functions of Langlands parameters (Shahidi, Ann. of Math. 132 (1990)), using the local Langlands correspondence for the Levi factors.

items.name: Proposition 10.2 (principal series of PGSp_6 induced from P_13)
items.statement: For τ ∈ Irr(GL_2), I_13(s, τ ⊗ 1) = Ind_{P_13}^{PGSp_6}((|det|^s τ) ⊗ 1), whose restriction to Sp_6 is induced from |·|^{2s} ω_τ ⊗ |det|^s τ. For τ unitary supercuspidal it is reducible if and only if τ^∨ ≅ τ and either ω_τ = 1 and s = ±1/2, when I_13(1/2, τ ⊗ 1) has length 4 with a unique irreducible submodule δ_13(τ), a generic discrete series; or ω_τ ≠ 1, Im(φ_τ) ≠ S_3 and s = 0, when I_13(0, τ ⊗ 1) = I_13(τ ⊗ 1)_gen ⊕ I_13(τ ⊗ 1)_deg.

items.name: Proposition 10.3 (principal series of PGSp_6 induced from P_3; Tadić)
items.statement: (i) For τ a discrete series representation of GL_3 with trivial central character, I_3(τ) = Ind_{P_3}^{PGSp_6} τ is irreducible if τ ≠ τ^∨ (and I_3(τ) ≅ I_3(τ^∨)), and I_3(τ) = I_3(τ)_gen ⊕ I_3(τ)_deg if τ ≅ τ^∨. (ii) For characters χ_1χ_2χ_3 = 1 and τ = τ(χ_1, χ_2, χ_3), I_3(τ) is irreducible unless χ_i = |·|^{±1} for some i or χ_i/χ_j = |·|^{±1} for some i ≠ j; or the χ_i are quadratic, nontrivial and pairwise different, when I_3(τ) = I_3(τ)_gen ⊕ I_3(τ)_deg.
items.note: Tadić, 'Representations of p-adic symplectic groups', Compos. Math. 90 (1994), Example 7.7 and Theorem 7.9.

items.name: Proposition 10.4 (principal series of PGSp_6 induced from P_1)
items.statement: Let τ be a supercuspidal representation of GSp_4(F) with trivial central character and L-parameter ϕ_τ : WD_F → Spin_5 ≅ Sp_4, such that std ∘ ϕ_τ contains the trivial representation (std the 5-dimensional representation). Then I_1(s, τ) = Ind_{P_1}^{PGSp_6} |ν|^s τ is reducible if and only if s = ±1/2, with 0 → δ_1(τ) → I_1(1/2, τ) → J_1(1/2, τ) → 0 and δ_1(τ) a discrete series representation.
items.note: Uses the local Langlands correspondence for GSp_4 (Gan–Takeda; item gsp4-llc).

items.name: The local Langlands correspondence for GSp_4 (Gan–Takeda)
items.statement: Irreducible representations of GSp_4(F) have L-parameters WD_F → GSp_4(C), with the properties of Gan–Takeda (Ann. of Math. 173 (2011)); for trivial central character the parameter lands in Spin_5 ≅ Sp_4(C).
items.note: Used to compute reducibility points for P_1 (Shahidi's method) and to state Proposition 10.4.

items.name: Some non-tempered representations of PGSp_6
items.statement: (a′) For τ as in (a) of item nontempered-g2, σ = τ ⊗ τ on M_2 ≅ GSO_4: I_2(σ) is a standard module with unique irreducible quotient J_2(τ ⊗ τ). (b′) For τ as in (b), σ = τ ⊗ 1 on M_13 ≅ GL_2 × GL_1: I_13(σ) is a standard module with unique irreducible quotient J_13(τ ⊗ 1). (c′) For τ as in (c), I_13(τ ⊗ 1) is a quotient of a standard module for the Borel subgroup and has a unique irreducible quotient J_13(τ ⊗ 1).

items.name: Proposition 11.1 and Corollary 11.2 (Whittaker periods; [GS04])
items.statement: Let Π be the minimal representation of E_7 and (V′, ψ′) a Whittaker datum for PGSp_6. Then Π_{V′,ψ′} ≅ ind_V^{G_2} ψ_V as G_2-modules, (V, ψ_V) a Whittaker datum for G_2. Hence (i) for generic π ∈ Irr(G_2), dim Hom_{V′}(Θ(π), ψ) = 1, so Θ(π) has a unique irreducible generic subquotient and is nonzero; (ii) for non-generic π ∈ Irr(G_2) and generic τ ∈ Irr(PGSp_6), Hom_{G_2 × PGSp_6}(Π, π ⊗ τ) = 0.
items.note: Gan–Savin 2004, Prop. 19 and Cor. 20; see also the appendix of Harris–Khare–Thorne.

items.name: The Fourier–Jacobi period of G_2
items.statement: With Q = LU and [L, L] ≅ SL_2 attached to the long simple root β, J = [L, L]U; J modulo the centre of U is the Jacobi group. ρ_ψ is the unique irreducible representation of the double cover J̃ on which the centre of U/[U, U] ≅ U_{2α+β} acts by ψ. For genuine σ ∈ Irr(S̃L_2), σ ⊗ ρ_ψ is a representation of J, and the Fourier–Jacobi period of π ∈ Irr(G_2) with respect to σ is Hom_J(π, σ ⊗ ρ_ψ) ≅ Hom_{G_2}(π, Ind_J^{G_2} σ ⊗ ρ_ψ).

items.name: Lemma 11.3 (enhanced uniqueness of the Fourier–Jacobi model)
items.statement: If π ∈ Irr(G_2) is generic and tempered (or has cuspidal support on Q), then Hom_{G_2}(ind_J^{G_2}(I_ψ(−s) ⊗ ρ_ψ̄), π^∨) ≅ Hom_{G_2}(π, Ind_J^{G_2}(I_ψ̄(s) ⊗ ρ_ψ)) ≅ C for all s < 1/2, where I_ψ(s) are the principal series of S̃L_2.
items.note: Proof: I_ψ̄(s) ⊗ ρ_ψ ≅ ind_{T_β N}^J(|·|^{s+3/2} ψ_{2α+β}); the Whittaker functional gives a unique copy of C_c(T_γ) in π_{U,ψ_α}; temperedness controls the exponents; root exchange (Lemma 11.4) moves from T_γ N′ to T_β N. The proof is written for tempered π; for cuspidal support on Q, π_N = 0 and the same argument goes through at once.

items.name: Lemma 11.4 (root exchange)
items.statement: Let H be a Heisenberg group, π a smooth H-module, X and Y maximal abelian subgroups, and ψ_X, ψ_Y characters agreeing on X ∩ Y and nontrivial on the centre of H. Then ℓ ↦ ℓ′, ℓ′(v) = ∫_{Y/X∩Y} ℓ(π(y)v) dy, is an isomorphism Hom_X(π, ψ_X) ≅ Hom_Y(π, ψ_Y).

items.name: The Shalika period of PGSp_6
items.statement: For a generic character ψ_2 of N_2 (the unipotent radical of P_2), its stabilizer in M_2 is PGL_2^Δ; the Shalika subgroup is S = PGL_2^Δ ⋉ N_2 with ψ_S extending ψ_2 trivially on PGL_2(F). The Shalika period of π is the coinvariant space π_{S,ψ_S}.

items.name: Twisted Jacquet modules of the minimal representations
items.statement: (i) (Π_J)_{N,ψ_E} ≅ ind_{H_{J,E}}^{H_J}(1) as H_J-modules (Gross–Savin, Compos. Math. 114 (1998), Lemma 2.9). (ii) For the minimal representation Π of E_7 and a Whittaker datum (V, ψ_V) of G_2, Π_{V,ψ_V} ≅ ind_S^{PGSp_6} ψ_S (Savin–Weissman, Compos. Math. 147 (2011), Lemma 4.5).
items.locator: Proofs of Lemmas 6.4 and 12.1; §11.3, Proposition 11.5, pp. 21–38 (arXiv v1)

items.name: The twisted Jacquet module Π_{N_2,ψ_2}
items.statement: For the minimal representation Π of E_7, Π_{N_2,ψ_2} ≅ ind_J^{G_2}(C_c(M_2°(F)) ⊗ ρ_ψ) as G_2 × PGL_2-modules, where PGL_2 acts on the trace-zero matrices M_2°(F) by conjugation, C_c(M_2°(F)) is the Weil representation of PGL_2 × S̃L_2 = SO_3 × S̃L_2, and PGL_2 acts trivially on ρ_ψ.
items.note: Stated ('Firstly, we have') with no proof or reference (sourceIssues E10).

items.name: Lemma 11.6 (isotypic quotients of compactly induced modules)
items.statement: Let H ⊂ G and L be p-adic groups, W a smooth H × L-module and τ ∈ Irr(L) with maximal τ-isotypic quotient Θ(τ) ⊗ τ of W. If Ext¹_L(τ, τ) = 0, then ind_H^G Θ(τ) ⊗ τ is the maximal τ-isotypic quotient of ind_H^G W (compact induction).

items.name: Proposition 11.7 (the Shalika period of the E_7 minimal representation)
items.statement: As a G_2(F)-representation, Π_{S,ψ_S} ≅ (Π_{N_2,ψ_2})_{PGL_2} ≅ ind_J^{G_2}(I_ψ̄(1/2) ⊗ ρ_ψ).
items.note: From item pi-n2-psi2, Lemma 11.6 with Ext¹_{PGL_2}(1, 1) = 0, and the identification of the PGL_2-coinvariants of C_c(M_2°(F)) with the full degenerate principal series I_ψ̄(1/2) of S̃L_2.

items.name: Lemma 12.1 (a second chain of containments)
items.statement: Let Π be the minimal representation of E_7, π ∈ Irr(G_2) tempered, ψ_V a Whittaker character of G_2, H = PGSp_6 and τ ∈ Irr(H) tempered with Hom_{G_2 × H}(Π, π ⊠ τ) ≠ 0. Then Hom_V(π, ψ_V) ⊆ Hom_V(Θ(τ), ψ_V) ≅ Hom_S(τ^∨, ψ̄_S) ⊆ Hom_S(Θ(π^∨), ψ̄_S) ≅ Hom_{G_2}(ind_J^{G_2} I_ψ(1/2) ⊗ ρ_ψ̄, π^∨). If π is generic, all these spaces are one-dimensional.

items.name: Proposition 12.2
items.statement: Let τ ∈ Irr(PGSp_6) be tempered. Then Θ(τ) cannot have two irreducible tempered generic quotients.
items.note: Savin–Weissman proved this from the uniqueness of Shalika functionals, whose proof is difficult; this proof uses only Lemma 11.3.

items.name: Proposition 12.3
items.statement: Let π ∈ Irr(G_2) be tempered and generic. Then Θ(π) cannot have two tempered irreducible quotients; in particular Θ(π)_c is irreducible or 0.

items.name: Theorem 12.4 (Howe duality for G_2 × PGSp_6, tempered case)
items.statement: Let π ∈ Irr(G_2) be tempered with big theta lift Θ(π) on PGSp_6. (i) Θ(π) has finite length and, if nonzero, a unique irreducible quotient θ(π), which is tempered. (ii) For tempered π_1, π_2 ∈ Irr(G_2), 0 ≠ θ(π_1) ≅ θ(π_2) implies π_1 ≅ π_2.
items.note: The proof cites 'Lemmas 6.2(i) and 6.3(ii)'; 6.3(i) is meant (sourceIssues E11).

items.name: Corollary 12.5
items.statement: Let π ∈ Irr(G_2) be generic, supercuspidal and not a theta lift from PGL_3. Then Θ(π) is generic, supercuspidal and irreducible.
items.note: Generic and supercuspidal by Savin–Weissman; irreducible by Proposition 12.3.

items.name: Proposition 13.1 (r_P of the E_7 minimal representation; Magaard–Savin)
items.statement: Let H = PGSp_6 and P ⊂ E_7 the parabolic subgroup with P ∩ G_2 = P (Levi of type D_6). As a GL_2 × H-module, the normalized Jacquet module r_P(Π) has a filtration with successive quotients (top to bottom): (1) δ_P^{−1/2} Π_N = Π_{D_6} |det|^{1/2} ⊕ Π_∅ |det|^{3/2}; (2) Ind_{B̄ × P_2}^{GL_2 × H}(δ · C_c(GL_1)), δ = |·|^{−1/2} × |·| on the lower triangular B̄; (3) Ind_{P_13}^H C_c(GL_2). The centre of M ≅ GL_2 acts trivially on Π_{D_6} and Π_∅ (the minimal and trivial representations of the Levi).
items.note: Magaard–Savin, 'Exceptional Θ-correspondences I', Compos. Math. 107 (1997), Th. 6.1.

items.name: Lemma 13.2 (the similitude theta correspondence for GL_2 × GSO_4)
items.statement: Let W be the Weil representation for the similitude dual pair GL_2 × GSO_4, GSO_4 ≅ (GL_2 × GL_2)/GL_1^∇ acting on M_2(F) by left and right multiplication. Its irreducible quotients are π^∨ ⊗ π ⊗ π. For an irreducible generic representation π of GL_2, Θ(π^∨) = π ⊗ π and Θ(π ⊗ π) = π^∨.
items.note: Proof via W_{V,ψ} = C_c(GL_2); the Steinberg case needs Ext¹_{SO_4}(1 ⊗ 1, st ⊗ st) = 0 and the action of the centre. The similitude theta correspondence is Roberts (Israel J. Math. 94 (1996)).

items.name: Proposition 13.3 (r_Q of the E_7 minimal representation)
items.statement: As a GL_2 × H-module, r_Q(Π) has a filtration with successive quotients (top to bottom): (1) δ_Q^{−1/2} Π_U = Π_{A_5} |det|^{3/2} ⊕ Π_{A_1} |det|²; (2) Ind_{B̄ × P_2}^{GL_2 × H}(δ · C_c(GL_1)), δ = |·|^{1/2} × |·|; (3) Ind_{P_2}^H W, W the Weil representation of Lemma 13.2. The centre of L ≅ GL_2 acts trivially on Π_{A_5} and Π_{A_1}.
items.note: Its proof is 'entirely similar' to Gan–Savin 1999, Prop. 6.8 (the non-split form of H), with δ fixed by a compatibility check ('an easy exercise').

items.name: Lemma 13.4 (theta lifts of non-tempered representations of G_2)
items.statement: Let π ∈ Irr(G_2) be non-tempered. If π ⊂ I_Q(τ^∨) with τ as in (a), then Θ(π) is a quotient of I_2(τ ⊗ τ), hence of finite length, and Θ(J_2(τ ⊗ τ)) ≠ 0. If π ⊂ I_P(τ^∨) with τ as in (b) or (c), then Θ(π) is a quotient of I_13(τ ⊗ 1), hence of finite length, and Θ(J_13(τ ⊗ 1)) ≠ 0.
items.note: Uses Θ(π)^* ≅ Hom_{G_2}(Π, π), the filtration of Proposition 13.3, second adjointness, the maximal isotypic quotient of Ind_{P_2}^H W (Gan–Gurevich, Lemma 9.4) and Lemma 13.2. The second case is 'completely analogous'.

items.name: Proposition 13.5 (r_{P_3} of the E_7 minimal representation; Magaard–Savin)
items.statement: As a G_2 × GL_3-module, r_{P_3}(Π) has a filtration with successive quotients (top to bottom): (1) δ_{P_3}^{−1/2} Π_{N_3} = Π_{E_6} ⊕ Π_∅ |det|; (2) Ind_{Q × Q_1}^{G_2 × GL_3}(δ · C_c(GL_1)), δ(g_1, g_2) = |g_1|^{−1/2} |det g_2|^{1/2}; (3) Ind_{P × Q_2}^{G_2 × GL_3}(C_c(GL_2)); here Q_1, Q_2 ⊂ GL_3 are the lower block-triangular parabolics stabilizing the row vectors (∗, 0, 0) and (∗, ∗, 0). The pieces (2) and (3) come from the two G_2 × GL_3-orbits Ω_1, Ω_2 on the null triples Ω ⊂ O_0³.
items.note: Magaard–Savin 1997, §5.

items.name: Proposition 13.6 (r_{P_1} of the E_7 minimal representation)
items.statement: As a G_2 × GSp_4-module, r_{P_1}(Π) has a filtration with successive quotients (top to bottom): (1) δ_{P_1}^{−1/2} Π_{N_1} = Π_{D_6} |ν|^{1/2} ⊕ Π_∅ |ν|^{3/2}; (2) Ind_{Q × Q_1}^{G_2 × GSp_4}(δ · C_c(GL_1)), δ(g_1, g_2) = |g_1|^{−1/2} |det g_2|^{1/2}; (3) Ind_{P × Q_2}^{G_2 × GSp_4}(C_c(GL_2)), Q_1, Q_2 ⊂ GSp_4 the stabilizers of (∗, 0, 0, 0) and (∗, ∗, 0, 0). The pieces come from the two orbits on the null quadruples Ω ⊂ O_0⁴ with x ∧ x′ + y ∧ y′ = 0.
items.note: 'This case is not in the literature; however, it is similar to' Savin–Woodbury (J. Number Theory 146 (2015), §5). The paper describes the orbits and states the result without proof (sourceIssues E13). The text also calls ν 'the similitude character of GSp_6' where GSp_4 is meant.

items.name: Proposition 13.7 (r_{P_2} of the E_7 minimal representation)
items.statement: As a G_2 × (GL_2 × GL_2)/GL_1^∇-module, r_{P_2}(Π) has a filtration with four successive quotients: (1) δ_{P_2}^{−1/2} Π_{N_2} = Π_{D_5} |det|^{1/2} ⊕ Π_{A_1} |det|^{3/2}; (2) Ind_{Q × (B̄ × B̄)/GL_1^∇}^{G_2 × M_2}(δ · C_c(GL_1)), δ = |·|^{1/2} × |·| on each B̄; (3) Ind_{P × B̄}^{G_2 × GL_2}(C_c(GL_2)), B̄ in the second GL_2 factor acting through the (1,1) entry; (4) Ind_Q^{G_2} W, W the Weil representation of GL_2 × GSO_4.
items.note: A combination of Gan–Savin 1999, Prop. 8.1 (the bottom piece), and the orbit analysis of the highest-weight orbit ω; the unknown twisting character δ′ is fixed by compatibility with Lemma 13.4. The notes to the proposition write M_3 for the Levi M_2 (sourceIssues E14).

items.name: Lemma 13.8 (theta lifts of non-tempered representations of PGSp_6)
items.statement: Let σ ∈ Irr(PGSp_6) be non-tempered. Then Θ(σ) = 0 unless σ is as in Lemma 13.4. If σ ⊂ I_2(τ^∨ ⊗ τ^∨), then Θ(σ) is a quotient of I_Q(τ), hence of finite length, and Θ(J_Q(τ)) ≠ 0. If σ ⊂ I_13(τ^∨ ⊗ 1), then Θ(σ) is a quotient of I_P(τ), hence of finite length, and Θ(J_P(τ)) ≠ 0.
items.note: The proof treats standard modules for P_2, P_23 and P_12 and leaves those for P_123, P_13, P_1 and P_3 'to the reader' (sourceIssues E12). It prints J_P(τ_1) for J_P(τ_2) (sourceIssues E15).

items.name: Theorem 14.1 (theta lifts of non-tempered representations)
items.statement: (a) Θ(J_Q(τ)) is a nonzero quotient of I_2(τ ⊗ τ), of finite length with unique irreducible quotient J_2(τ ⊗ τ); Θ(J_2(τ ⊗ τ)) is a nonzero quotient of I_Q(τ) with unique irreducible quotient J_Q(τ). (b) Θ(J_P(τ)) is a nonzero quotient of I_13(τ ⊗ 1) with unique irreducible quotient J_13(τ ⊗ 1); Θ(J_13(τ ⊗ 1)) is a nonzero quotient of I_P(τ) with unique irreducible quotient J_P(τ). (c) Θ(σ) = 0 for every other non-tempered σ ∈ Irr(PGSp_6). In particular, if π ⊗ σ is a quotient of Π, then π is non-tempered if and only if σ is.
items.note: The last sentence prints 'π ⊗ τ' for π ⊗ σ (sourceIssues E16).

items.name: Proposition 14.2 (finiteness for G_2 × SO_{2n−7} ⊂ SO_{2n})
items.statement: Let Π_n be the minimal representation of SO(2n), n = 5 or 6. For tempered π ∈ Irr(G_2), Θ_n(π) is a finite-length H_n-module, H_n = SO_{2n−7}.
items.note: Proof: Π_n is the big theta lift of the trivial representation of SL_2 (Yamana, Israel J. Math. 185 (2011), Prop. 8.4, for irreducibility); a see-saw gives Θ_n(π)^* ≅ Hom_{S̃L_2}(Ω_{2n−7,ψ}, Θ̃_ψ(π)) (14.3); finiteness of Θ̃_ψ(π) for S̃L_2 × G_2 follows from Gan–Gurevich (Amer. J. Math. 128 (2006), Prop. 8.1 and Th. 9.1(c),(d)) and classical Howe duality.

items.name: The theta correspondence for S̃L_2 × G_2 (Gan–Gurevich)
items.statement: For the dual pair S̃L_2 × G_2 ⊂ S̃L_2 × SO_7 in the Weil representation Ω_ψ: (a) Ω_N sits in 0 → Ind_Q^{G_2} C_c(GL_1) → Ω_N → C → 0 (L ≅ GL_2 acting on GL_1 through det); (b) for genuine supercuspidal σ_1 ≇ σ_2 of S̃L_2, θ̃_ψ(σ_1) ≇ θ̃_ψ(σ_2); (c) (Lemma 15.4) for each supercuspidal ρ of PGL_2, with JL(ρ) its Jacquet–Langlands transfer to PB^× = SO_3^* (B the quaternion division algebra) and σ_ρ the ψ-theta lift of JL(ρ) to S̃L_2 (an irreducible genuine supercuspidal), π_ρ := θ(σ_ρ) ∈ Irr(G_2) is nonzero irreducible supercuspidal with Θ(π_ρ) = σ_ρ; ρ ↦ π_ρ is injective on supercuspidals; and every supercuspidal π of G_2 that lifts to S̃L_2 but not to PGL_3 or PD^× is some π_ρ.
items.note: Gan–Gurevich, 'Nontempered A-packets of G_2: liftings from S̃L_2', Amer. J. Math. 128 (2006), Prop. 8.1, Lemma 9.4 and Th. 9.1. The paper's bibliography gives volume 170 and the note 'finiteness of Θ̃_ψ(π) was not formally stated there'. In (c) the paper prints 'an isotropic inner form' and 'JL(τ)' (sourceIssues E17).

items.name: Theorem 15.1 (Howe duality for G_2 × PGSp_6)
items.statement: Let π ∈ Irr(G_2). (i) Θ(π) ≠ 0 if and only if π has zero theta lift to PD^×. (ii) If Θ(π) ≠ 0, it has finite length and a unique irreducible quotient θ(π). (iii) θ(π_1) ≅ θ(π_2) ≠ 0 implies π_1 ≅ π_2. (iv) If Θ(π) ≠ 0, θ(π) is tempered if and only if π is. (v) If π is non-tempered, θ(π) ≠ 0 and its L-parameter is that of π composed with G_2(C) ⊂ Spin_7(C).
items.note: Combines Theorem 12.4 and Theorem 14.1.

items.name: Theorem 15.2 (lifts to PGSp_6 of lifts from PGL_3)
items.statement: Let π ∈ Irr(G_2) be tempered with π = θ_B(τ^ε) for a tempered τ ∈ Irr(PGL_3). (i) If τ ≇ τ^∨, θ(π) ≅ I_3(τ) ≅ I_3(τ^∨) ∈ Irr(PGSp_6). (ii) If τ ≅ τ^∨ and the parameter of τ contains a trivial summand, θ(π) ≅ I_3(τ). (iii) If τ ≅ τ^∨ and the parameter has no trivial summand, then π is π_gen = θ_B(τ^+) or π_deg = θ_B(τ^−), I_3(τ) = I_3(τ)_gen ⊕ I_3(τ)_deg, θ(π_gen) = I_3(τ)_gen and θ(π_deg) = I_3(τ)_deg.
items.note: The facts listed before it cite 'Theorem 15.1(v)' for the tempered case, where 15.1(ii) and (iv) are meant (sourceIssues E18).

items.name: Theorem 15.3 (lifts of the remaining tempered non-supercuspidal representations)
items.statement: Let π ∈ Irr(G_2) be tempered and not a lift from PGL_3. (i) For τ a unitary discrete series representation of GL_2, I_Q(τ) is irreducible if and only if I_2(τ ⊗ τ) is; then θ(I_Q(τ)) ≅ I_2(τ ⊗ τ), and otherwise θ(I_Q(τ)_gen) ≅ I_2(τ ⊗ τ)_gen and θ(I_Q(τ)_deg) ≅ I_2(τ ⊗ τ)_deg. (ii) For τ ≅ τ^∨ supercuspidal with trivial central character, θ(δ_Q(τ)) ≅ δ_2(τ) and θ(δ_P(τ)) ≅ δ_13(τ). (iii) For τ ≅ τ^∨ supercuspidal with parameter of image S_3, θ(π_gen[τ]) ≅ σ_gen[τ]. (iv) For χ² = 1 ≠ χ, θ(π_gen[χ]) ≅ σ_gen[χ]. (v) θ(St_{G_2}) = St_{PGSp_6}.
items.note: Stated without a written proof; the paper derives the explicit lifts from four listed facts: Theorem 15.1(i), temperedness and irreducibility, non-genericity (Corollary 11.2(ii)) and cuspidal supports from §13.

items.name: The Saito–Kurokawa representations τ_ρ of SO_5
items.statement: For σ_ρ as in Lemma 15.4, τ_ρ = Θ(σ_ρ) = θ(σ_ρ) ∈ Irr(SO_5) is its ψ-theta lift from S̃L_2 to SO_5: a nongeneric supercuspidal representation of SO_5 in a Saito–Kurokawa A-packet.

items.name: Lemma 15.5
items.statement: Restrict the minimal representation of SO_12 to G_2 × SO_5. Then for ρ ∈ Irr_sc(PGL_2), Θ(π_ρ) = τ_ρ.
items.note: From the see-saw identity (14.3) and Lemma 15.4(i): Θ(π_ρ)^* ≅ Hom_{S̃L_2}(Ω_5, σ_ρ) = τ_ρ^*.

items.name: Proposition 15.6 (lifts of supercuspidals that do not come from PGL_3 or PD^×)
items.statement: Let π ∈ Irr(G_2) be supercuspidal and not a lift from PGL_3 or PD^×. If π = π_ρ for some ρ ∈ Irr_sc(PGL_2), then θ(π_ρ) = δ_1(τ_ρ), the square-integrable subquotient of I_1(1/2, τ_ρ) (Proposition 10.4). Otherwise θ(π) is supercuspidal.

items.name: Corollary 15.7 (the discrete series trichotomy)
items.statement: If π ∈ Irr(G_2) is a discrete series representation that does not lift to PGL_3 or PD^×, then θ(π) is an irreducible discrete series representation of PGSp_6. Hence every discrete series representation of G_2 lifts to a discrete series representation of exactly one of PD^×, PGL_3 and PGSp_6, and the lift is Whittaker generic if and only if π is.

items.name: Tools from smooth representation theory
items.statement: For p-adic groups and smooth representations: Frobenius reciprocity for induction and compact induction; Mackey theory for restricting induced representations; Jacquet modules and Bernstein's second adjointness; the Bernstein decomposition into cuspidal and noncuspidal parts; the Langlands classification of non-tempered irreducibles as unique quotients of standard modules; and Casselman's criterion for temperedness by the exponents of Jacquet modules.
items.note: SR.2 plans induction, Frobenius reciprocity, Mackey filtrations and Jacquet functors; SR.2a second adjointness; SR.3 the Bernstein decomposition and the matrix-coefficient criteria for temperedness. The Langlands classification for p-adic groups is not named in SR.

items.name: Semisimplicity of cuspidal parts and projectivity of discrete series
items.statement: For a p-adic reductive group with compact centre (G_2, PGSp_6, PGL_3, PD^×), the cuspidal component of any smooth representation is semisimple; and discrete series representations are projective in the category of tempered representations.
items.locator: §1 and proof of Proposition 5.3, pp. 4–18 (arXiv v1)
items.note: Both are used without reference: the first to give Θ(π)_c an irreducible quotient, the second for Ext¹(π_deg[1], π) = 0 with π tempered. The second is a theorem of Meyer on the tempered category.

items.name: The local Langlands correspondence for general linear groups
items.statement: The local Langlands correspondence for GL_n(F), used for the Levi factors GL_2, GL_1 × GL_1 of G_2 and GL_3, GSO_4 of PGSp_6, and to attach L-parameters φ_τ to τ ∈ Irr(PGL_3).

items.name: Weil representations of S̃L_2 and theta lifts to O_3
items.statement: The Weil representation ρ_ψ of S̃L_2 decomposes as ρ_ψ^+ ⊕ ρ_ψ^− (even and odd). For the Weil representation of O_3 × S̃L_2 on C_c(M_2°(F)) (determinant form), the theta lift of ρ_ψ^− to O_3 is st^− and that of ρ_ψ^+ is the principal series with trivial quotient and submodule st^+ (st^± the extensions of the Steinberg representation of SO_3 ≅ PGL_2 with −1 acting by ±1). The principal series I_ψ(s) of S̃L_2 satisfy 0 → St_ψ → I_ψ(1/2) → ρ_ψ^+ → 0, and I_ψ(1/2)^∨ = I_ψ̄(−1/2); the PGL_2-coinvariants of C_c(M_2°(F)) are the full I_ψ̄(1/2).
items.note: Classical theta for S̃L_2 × O_3 (Waldspurger), used without proof.

items.name: Classical Howe duality inputs
items.statement: Howe duality for the classical dual pairs used in §14: S̃L_2 × SO_{2n−7}, the similitude pair GL_2 × GSO_4, and Sp(V_2′) × Sp(V_2) → SO(V_2′ ⊗ V_2); in particular big theta lifts there have finite length.
items.note: The same theorem PAPER-GAN-ICHINO-18 routed to MP.3 (Gan–Takeda; Waldspurger; Howe); the similitude version is Roberts.

items.name: The minimal representation of SO_2n as a theta lift
items.statement: The minimal representation of SO_2n (n = 5, 6) is the big theta lift of the trivial representation of SL_2, and this lift is irreducible (Yamana, Israel J. Math. 185 (2011), Prop. 8.4).

prerequisites.citation: W. T. Gan and G. Savin, On minimal representations: definitions and properties, Represent. Theory 9 (2005), 46–93
prerequisites.why: Minimal representations of the groups G_J and the Lie algebras g_J (§4).

prerequisites.citation: K. Magaard and G. Savin, Exceptional Θ-correspondences I, Compos. Math. 107 (1997), 89–123
prerequisites.why: Jacquet modules of the E_7 minimal representation (Propositions 13.1 and 13.5).

prerequisites.why: (Π_J)_{N,ψ_E} ≅ ind_{H_{J,E}}^{H_J}(1) (Lemma 2.9), used in Lemma 6.4.

prerequisites.citation: G. Savin, A class of supercuspidal representations of G_2(k), Canad. Math. Bull. 42 (1999), 393–400
prerequisites.why: The correspondence for PD^× × G_2 (Proposition 7.1).

prerequisites.why: The Jacquet-module filtrations adapted in Propositions 13.3 and 13.7.

routes.title: Exceptional theta correspondences for G_2: minimal representations, Howe duality and theta dichotomy
routes.brief: A new roadmap for the exceptional theta correspondences of Gan–Savin, 'Howe duality and dichotomy for exceptional theta correspondences' (Invent. Math. 232 (2023); arXiv:2102.00372). The roadmap covers the restriction of minimal representations of adjoint groups of type E to the dual pairs PD^× × G_2 ⊂ E_6^D, (PGL_3 ⋊ Z/2Z) × G_2 ⊂ E_6 ⋊ Z/2Z and G_2 × PGSp_6 ⊂ E_7 over a p-adic field F of characteristic 0 (D a cubic division algebra). Final theorems, as the paper states them. Theorem 1.1 (dichotomy): every π ∈ Irr(G_2(F)) has nonzero theta lift to exactly one of PD^× and PGSp_6(F). Theorem 1.2 (Howe duality): for π_1, π_2 ∈ Irr(G_2(F)), Θ(π_i) has finite length and dim Hom_{H_J}(θ(π_1), θ(π_2)) ≤ dim Hom_{G_2}(π_1, π_2); for τ ∈ Irr(H_J), Θ(τ) has finite length with a unique irreducible quotient if nonzero. There are injections θ_D : Irr^♥(PD^×) ↪ Irr(G_2) (with Irr^♥(PD^×) = Irr(PD^×) if p ≠ 3), θ_B : Irr^♥(PGL_3 ⋊ Z/2Z) ↪ Irr(G_2) with image disjoint from that of θ_D, and θ : Irr(G_2) ∖ Im θ_D ↪ Irr(PGSp_6). Theorem 1.3: the correspondences preserve temperedness; every discrete series of G_2 lifts to a discrete series of exactly one of PD^×, PGL_3 ⋊ Z/2Z and PGSp_6; and they are functorial on non-tempered representations. The explicit lifts of Theorems 8.2, 8.5, 14.1, 15.1–15.3, Proposition 15.6 and Corollary 15.7 are also final results. Cover, in this order: (1) the split octonions (import Tau Ceti's Octonion) and G_2 = Aut(O), identified with the split Chevalley group of type G_2, with its parabolic subgroups P and Q, SL_3 ⊂ G_2 and the needed facts about G_2(C); (2) representations of p-adic G_2: Muić's reducibility results (Propositions 3.1–3.3), the Langlands classification of the non-tempered representations, the partial local Langlands correspondence of §3.4, and degenerate Whittaker models along N indexed by cubic algebras (Mœglin–Waldspurger, Varma; Lemma 3.4); (3) Freudenthal–Jordan algebras of dimension 1, 3, 9 and 15, the Lie algebras g_J and groups G_J (including E_6^D and Spin_8^E), the dual pairs G_2 × Aut(J) and Aut(i : E → J) × Spin_8^E, and the see-saw; (4) minimal representations Π_J and big theta lifts, with the twisted Jacquet modules the proofs use and the Jacquet-module filtrations of §13 (Magaard–Savin, Gross–Savin, Savin, Gan–Savin, Savin–Weissman); (5) the degenerate principal series I_E(s) of Spin_8^E, the representations R_J(E), the Mackey filtration of I_E(s) restricted to G_2, and the Ext vanishing of §5; (6) the dichotomy theorem (§6); (7) PD^× × G_2 (§7, with Savin's results and Lonka–Tandon); (8) (PGL_3 ⋊ Z/2Z) × G_2 (§8, with Gan–Savin 2004); (9) the representations of PGSp_6 that are needed (§§9–10, principal series from P_1, P_2, P_3 and P_13, after Tadić and Gan–Takeda) and the Fourier–Jacobi and Shalika periods and root exchange of §11; (10) Howe duality for G_2 × PGSp_6 (§§12–15), with the auxiliary pairs G_2 × SO_{2n−7} ⊂ SO_{2n} and S̃L_2 × G_2 (Gan–Gurevich). Treat the steps the paper leaves open (sourceIssues E10, E12, E13 and E20–E22) as proof obligations. They are: Proposition 5.4; Lemmas 8.1 and 8.3; the computation of Π_{N_2,ψ_2}; Proposition 13.6; the cases left to the reader in Lemma 13.8 and §14.3; and the explicit lifts of Theorems 15.2–15.3. The published version, which was not accessible, may supply some of them. Design the roadmap so that PAPER-GAN-SAVIN-23-B, the local Langlands correspondence for G_2 built on this paper, can extend it. Import from: Smooth representations of local groups (SmoothRepresentationsOfLocalGroups) SR.2, SR.2a and SR.3. Metaplectic groups, Weil representations and automorphic theta kernels (MetaplecticAutomorphicForms) MP.2–MP.3, for classical Weil representations and classical Howe duality; this extraction routes those inputs to MP.3. Modularity, automorphy and Langlands endpoint extensions (ModularityAndLanglandsExtensions) ML.4, for the local Langlands correspondences of classical groups (GSp_4, Sp_6). Endoscopic transfer and unitary trace comparison (EndoscopicTransferAndUnitaryTraceComparison) ET.6, for GL_n and the inner form PD^×. Representations of semisimple Lie algebras, highest weight theory, and the Weyl formulas (tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/RepresentationTheory/LieHighestWeight) Layer 8, for the split octonions and the exceptional Lie algebras. Clifford algebras, the Pin and Spin groups, and spin representations (tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/RepresentationTheory/SpinRepresentations) Layer 8, for triality. Reductive algebraic groups (tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/ReductiveGroups) Layer 9, for the split Chevalley groups of types G_2, E_6 and E_7.
routes.reason: Nothing in the atlas plans exceptional groups over p-adic fields, minimal representations or exceptional dual pairs, and nothing plans the representation theory of p-adic G_2. The nearest roadmaps plan classical theta correspondences for the Weil representation (MetaplecticAutomorphicForms), smooth representation theory in general (SmoothRepresentationsOfLocalGroups), and the split octonions and exceptional Lie algebras over a characteristic-0 field (Tau Ceti's LieHighestWeight, Layer 8). None goes in this direction, so a Part II of any of them would stretch its scope. The roadmap imports those roadmaps and is designed for its only queued consumer, the local Langlands correspondence for G_2 (PAPER-GAN-SAVIN-23-B).

The paper also uses classical theta correspondences, which MP.3 owns: the Weil representations of S̃L_2 and their lifts to O_3, Howe duality for classical and similitude dual pairs, the similitude correspondence for GL_2 × GSO_4 (Lemma 13.2, proved in the paper), and the minimal representation of SO_2n as the theta lift of the trivial representation of SL_2. PAPER-GAN-ICHINO-18 routed classical Howe duality to MP.3 as well.

Two facts about the category of smooth representations are used without reference. For groups with compact centre, cuspidal parts are semisimple; and discrete series are projective in the tempered category. Both concern the Bernstein decomposition and temperedness, which SR.3 plans.
The local Langlands correspondence for GSp_4 (Gan–Takeda) is a classification input for a classical similitude group, the kind of input ML.4 owns. Here it computes reducibility points for P_1.

sourceIssues.printed: “This looks like a D_3 root system; however, the Weyl-invariant quadratic form in this case is q(s_1, s_2, s_3) = s_1² + s_2² + s_3³ − ¼(s_1 + s_2 + s_3)² rather than the usual dot product, and with this form, we have a realization of the C_3 root system with simple roots α_1 = (0, 1, −1), α_2 = (1, −1, 0), α_3 = (0, 2, 2).”
sourceIssues.correction: On the space of characters (s_1, s_2, s_3), where the paper has just written the Weyl action, the invariant form is s_1² + s_2² + s_3² + (s_1 + s_2 + s_3)², and the simple roots are (0, 1, −1), (1, −1, 0), (−1, 1, 1), of type C_3. The printed form, with s_3² for the misprinted s_3³, is the invariant form on the dual space of cocharacters (u_1, u_2, u_3). There the vectors (0, 1, −1), (1, −1, 0), (0, 2, 2) are the images 2α^∨/q(α^∨) of the simple roots, and α_3^∨ = (0, 1, 1).
sourceIssues.reason: The paper's reflection for α_3 is r_3(s) = (s_1 + s_2 + s_3, −s_3, −s_2), which is s − ⟨s, α_3^∨⟩α_3 with α_3^∨ = (0, 1, 1) and α_3 = (−1, 1, 1). The computation gives q(r_3 s) − q(s) = (5/4)((s_1 + s_2 + s_3)² − s_1²) ≠ 0, so q is not invariant on characters. A form a|s|² + b(Σs)² is invariant under r_1, r_2, r_3 exactly when a = b. Its inverse matrix I − J/4 gives the printed q on cocharacters. With the roots (0, 1, −1), (1, −1, 0), (−1, 1, 1) and the printed coroots, the Cartan matrix is [[2, −1, 0], [−1, 2, −1], [0, −2, 2]], of type C_3. All this was checked by computation in exact arithmetic. The positive chamber stated next, Re s_1 > Re s_2 > |Re s_3|, is correct, and nothing later uses q.
